solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Writer of Spanish verse can’t go wrong (9)

indicatorNotes.go wrong: the letters of the fodder go astray into a new order

annotation.surface: A poet boasting that their Spanish verse is foolproof.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in can’t is ignored, as punctuation always is. The definition reaches through to 'Spanish', so the surface's verse turns out to be Don Quixote's author.
annotation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes, author of Don Quixote, is the great writer in Spanish.

entries.clue: Soft copper nervous around others (5)

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
shy = ill at ease in company

annotation.surface: A timid policeman who goes easy on people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a policeman, and 'around' looks like a container signal, but it belongs to the phrase defining SHY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of easy and comfortable, as in a soft option.

entries.clue: Herring cleaner’s after money from America (7)

indicatorNotes.after: the cleaner comes after the money in the answer

blocks.note: a roll is American slang for a wad of banknotes

annotation.surface: A cleaner chasing an American payment.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is': the cleaner is after the money, so MOP goes second.
annotation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a rolled pickled herring fillet.

entries.clue: Deal with personal hygiene matter correctly as a help with contacts (7,4)

blocks.note: to address a problem is to deal with it

annotation.surface: Someone told to sort out their body odour if they want to network.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contacts' reads as social or business connections, which it is; the joke is that BO would scare them off.
annotation.definitionFit: An address book keeps the details of the people you contact.

entries.clue: Test something unknown found in fish (3,3)

indicatorNotes.found in: the unknown sits inside the fish

blocks.note: the trout is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: A lab testing a mystery substance discovered in fish.
annotation.walkthrough: Mathematicians use x, y and z for unknowns, and crosswords borrow any of the three.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to put something through a trial run, a plain synonym for test.

entries.clue: Avalanche — a sign spring is on its way? (8)

annotation.definition2: a sign spring is on its way

blocks.note: read cryptically, an avalanche is a drop of snow

blocks.clueFragment: a sign spring is on its way
blocks.note: a small white flower that blooms at the end of winter

annotation.surface: Wondering whether an avalanche means winter is ending.
annotation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: the word SNOWDROP split in two describes an avalanche.
annotation.definitionFit: Snowdrops are the first flowers of the year, a herald of spring.

entries.clue: Artificial wetlands surrounding you (5)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: the wetlands go round the you

blocks.note: the plural S of BOGS closes round the U

annotation.surface: A fake marsh built around the visitor.
annotation.walkthrough: U for 'you' is a standard crossword abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something sham or counterfeit rather than genuine.

entries.clue: One that might have a flutter in club (3)

annotation.definition: One that might have a flutter

blocks.clueFragment: One that might have a flutter
blocks.note: a flying mammal whose wings flutter
a club for striking a ball, as in cricket or baseball

annotation.surface: A gambler having a small bet at a club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Have a flutter' is British for placing a small bet, so the surface puts you in a gaming club; the flutter is really a bat's wings.
annotation.definitionFit: A bat flies with a fluttering wingbeat, and a cricket or baseball bat is a club.

entries.clue: City managed promotion in key area (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the managed promotion goes inside the key and area

annotation.surface: A city that ran an advertising push in an important district.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as important; here it is a musical key, one of the letters A to G.
annotation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia, home of the Alhambra.

entries.clue: Crop Ceres won’t fancy (9)

indicatorNotes.fancy: as an adjective, fancy = elaborately rearranged

annotation.surface: The Roman harvest goddess turning up her nose at a crop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb (Ceres won't like it); it is the anagram signal. Ceres is the goddess of grain, so maize is just what she should fancy.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: maize grown for its sweet kernels is one crop among many.

entries.clue: Spotted mole outside country house briefly (7)

indicatorNotes.outside: the mole goes outside the house
indicatorNotes.briefly: the word is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: a mole is a spy planted in an organisation
LODGE, a country house, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone spotted a mole outside a stately home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as seen; it is the adjective, covered in blotches. The mole is the espionage kind, not the burrowing one.
annotation.definitionFit: Splodgy means marked with splodges, i.e. spotted.

entries.clue: Blooming newspaper leading European anger (7)

indicatorNotes.leading: the newspaper goes in front of the European

blocks.note: flowers that are out are blooming
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

annotation.surface: A furious newspaper stirring up European fury.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' reads as the British mild swear word (blooming newspaper!); it is flowering.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though stronger: the fierce anger provoked by a scandal or injustice.

entries.clue: What’s eaten by many Americans? (3)

indicatorNotes.eaten by: the answer is swallowed inside the following words

annotation.surface: A question about a staple American food.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: yams, as sweet potatoes, are a Thanksgiving favourite in the US.
annotation.definitionFit: Americans eat yams (sweet potatoes) in quantity, especially at Thanksgiving.

entries.clue: Horse perhaps quickly prepared to throw first knight just as far? (11)

indicatorNotes.to throw first: to throw out the first knight is to drop the first N

blocks.note: an equid is any member of the horse family

blocks.clueFragment: quickly prepared to throw first knight
blocks.note: INSTANT (quickly prepared, as instant coffee) minus its first N, knight in chess notation

annotation.surface: A horse ready to unseat its rider so as to cover the same distance.
annotation.walkthrough: The horse throwing a knight is a riding picture; the knight is N from chess notation, and only the first of INSTANT's two Ns goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Equidistant means at equal distance, just as far.

entries.clue: Shaken with thief waving weapon (6,5)

indicatorNotes.waving: the letters wave about into a new order

annotation.surface: A rattled victim facing a thief brandishing a weapon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shaken' looks like the anagram signal; it is fodder, joined to THIEF by 'with', and 'waving' does the stirring.
annotation.definitionFit: A sheath knife is a fixed-blade knife carried in a sheath.

entries.clue: Uncover error by Chambers in Early English (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the error and chambers go inside Early English

blocks.note: first E of EE, the abbreviation for Early English

annotation.surface: Finding a mistake in the Chambers dictionary's treatment of Early English.
annotation.walkthrough: Chambers is a famous British dictionary, the surface's red herring; here chambers are chamber pots, POs from French pot.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lay bare, whether a body or a scandal.

entries.clue: Hopeful, still living outside quiet central London zone (9)

indicatorNotes.outside: still living goes outside quiet and the London zone

blocks.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

annotation.surface: Someone surviving on the edge of a peaceful district of central London, still optimistic.
annotation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the postal district covering the City of London.
annotation.definitionFit: Expectant means hopeful, expecting something.

entries.clue: Muse following second Democrat’s going with reasonable speed (8)

indicatorNotes.following: the muse comes after the second and the Democrat

blocks.note: a mo = a moment, a second
Erato is the Muse of love poetry

annotation.surface: A politician taking a moment to think over whether to move on.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', joining wordplay to the definition. 'Muse' reads as a verb, to ponder; it is one of the nine Muses.
annotation.definitionFit: Moderato is the musical direction to play at a moderate pace.

entries.clue: One may need a push to enter disreputable bordello (8)

annotation.definition: One may need a push to enter

indicatorNotes.disreputable: the letters are not in their proper, respectable order

annotation.surface: A shy customer needing encouragement to go into a brothel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A push' reads as a nudge of encouragement; it is a press of the button.
annotation.definitionFit: A doorbell is pushed by a visitor wanting to be let in.

entries.clue: A top zoo desperately holding river animals in a single cell (8)

indicatorNotes.desperately: the letters are thrown about wildly
indicatorNotes.holding: the rearranged letters hold the river

blocks.note: R = river, inserted after the P

annotation.surface: A top zoo desperately trying to keep its animals caged.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as best; it is only letters. R for river is a standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Protozoa are single-celled organisms once classed as animals.

entries.clue: Labour’s abandoned place for testing speech-making (7)

indicatorNotes.abandoned: Labour is left out of the word

blocks.note: a laboratory is where things are tested

annotation.surface: The Labour party dropping a venue where it rehearses its speeches.
annotation.walkthrough: Lab is the standard short form of Labour, the British political party.
annotation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of public speaking.

entries.clue: Position lacking over common drug (6)

indicatorNotes.lacking: the word is missing a letter

blocks.note: O, over in cricket scoring, removed

annotation.surface: A patient without the right post being overprescribed a routine medicine.
annotation.walkthrough: O for over comes from cricket scorecards.
annotation.definitionFit: Statins are cholesterol-lowering drugs taken by millions.

entries.clue: Agony of men — millions in temporary accommodation (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the men and millions go inside the tent

blocks.note: first letter of TENT, temporary accommodation

annotation.surface: Millions of men suffering in refugee camps.
annotation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) as 'men' is a crossword staple from the army: soldiers who are not officers.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for intense mental or physical suffering.

entries.clue: Fish served up in West Indian spicy paste (6)

indicatorNotes.served up: in a down clue, up means written bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: the fish goes inside West and Indian

annotation.surface: Fish served in a hot West Indian sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'West Indian' looks like a cuisine; it splits into W and I. Wasabi is Japanese, so the Caribbean picture misleads.
annotation.definitionFit: Wasabi is the hot green paste served with sushi.

entries.clue: Excellent joke card’s written about old queen (11)

indicatorNotes.written about: joke and card are written around the queen

blocks.note: the jack is a playing card

annotation.surface: A funny greeting card with a gag about an old queen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Card' reads as a greeting card, or a joker; it is the jack. The ’s stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Crackerjack is informal for excellent, first-rate.

entries.clue: Crustacean’s innards not at all cooked (3)

indicatorNotes.innards: the insides of the word, without its outer letters

annotation.surface: The guts of a shellfish served uncooked.
annotation.walkthrough: The crustacean is not named; PRAWN is the one whose middle letters fit. The ’s joins it to 'innards'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: food straight from the source, before any heat.

entries.clue: Flamingo possibly with a scarlet back? (5)

annotation.definition: Flamingo possibly with a scarlet back?

blocks.note: scarlet is a red, which goes back to DER

annotation.surface: Wondering whether a flamingo is red on its back.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a flamingo is a pink-red wading bird. Only the scarlet goes back: W, A, then RED reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a wader, a long-legged bird feeding in shallow water.

entries.clue: One of twelve letters in “some pub drink” (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the letters go inside the drink

blocks.note: first letter of ALE, some pub drink
the post is the letters delivered

annotation.surface: A spelling puzzle about a phrase in quotation marks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letters' reads as the alphabet, suggesting something hidden in the quoted words; it is mail. The quotes are there to make you look for a hidden answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Jesus chose twelve apostles.

entries.clue: One only just running to time (3)

annotation.surface: A train or runner barely keeping to schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Only just running to time' sounds like a late train; the definition is a toddler who has only just learnt to run.
annotation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child, one only just able to run.

entries.clue: Strong flavour I recognise in unwrapped American sweets (7)

indicatorNotes.in: I recognise goes inside the sweets
indicatorNotes.unwrapped: the word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: CANDY, American for sweets, without its outer letters gives AND; this is its start

annotation.surface: Someone identifying a strong taste in unwrapped American candy.
annotation.walkthrough: Unwrapping a word strips its first and last letters, just as you would a sweet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the seed of the anise plant gives a powerful liquorice taste.

entries.clue: Judge succeeded with tense meeting (5)

annotation.surface: A judge who has pulled off a nervy encounter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense meeting' reads as a strained encounter; tense is only T.
annotation.definitionFit: A tryst is a (usually secret) meeting of lovers.

entries.clue: Queen Elizabeth’s favourite location (9)

blocks.note: Robert Dudley, the earl who was Elizabeth I's favourite courtier
a city in the English Midlands

annotation.surface: Asking where the Queen liked best to be.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a place; the first definition is a person, the Earl of Leicester, Elizabeth I's favourite courtier.
annotation.definitionFit: The Earl of Leicester was Elizabeth I's favourite, and Leicester is a place.
